LEDE: Achievement Distillation (Moon et al., NeurIPS 2023) is the strongest published model-free agent on Crafter. We trained it and its PPO baseline for the standard 1M environment steps on a Windows laptop with an RTX 3050 and 4 GB of GPU memory, then added one change of our own: extra reward for achievements the agent rarely gets. Over three seeds it lifts PPO from 15.8 to 21.0. On Achievement Distillation it lifts our seed from 17.7 to 23.1, above the paper's 21.8.
RESULT_TEXT: The charts and tree below compare the seed-0 runs. Seed 0 is a weak seed for the baselines: PPO scores 12.4 there, against 16.7 and 18.2 on seeds 1 and 2, and AD scores 17.7 against the paper's 21.8. Both baselines get stuck at the stone pickaxe on this seed, which locks them out of iron. The rarity bonus breaks that wall: with AD and β = 2, stone pickaxes go from 1.6% of episodes to 25%, iron from 0.2% to 5.6%, and defeated skeletons from 15% to 23%. The next table shows how much of the gain holds across seeds.
FINDINGS:
180 → 1,620 steps/s

World generation was the bottleneck

Resetting Crafter took about a second, because world generation calls a pure-Python noise function 82,000 times. Early episodes last ~170 steps and the 8 environments step in lockstep, so resets stalled everything. Installing numba, which the noise library uses automatically, cut a reset to 50 ms. The generated maps are bit-identical.

4.3 GB → 2.2 GB

The paper's batch does not fit in 4 GB

A 512-sample minibatch needs 4.3 GB in fp32. Windows then pages GPU memory to system RAM instead of failing, and training runs 15× slower. Each minibatch is now split into two halves whose gradients are summed, which gives the same update.

934 s → ~600 s

The distillation phase repeated work

Every 8 rollouts AD trains 6 epochs on its contrastive losses. The official loop re-runs the frozen old policy on every sample in every epoch, encodes the same goal frames once per time step, and makes 16 tiny GPU calls per trajectory. Doing each once gives the same losses and gradients (relative difference 2.7e-5 in exact fp32) and is 1.7× faster.

85% VRAM cap

Silent memory paging

The first fast version was slower than the original. Memory cached from the PPO phase plus the aux phase's varied batch shapes pushed past 4 GB, and Windows paged the excess. Capping PyTorch at 85% of VRAM and clearing its cache before the aux phase fixed it.

same seed, different game

Crafter is not bit-reproducible

Creatures are stored in Python sets ordered by memory address, and the game picks which zombie to despawn from that order. A fixed seed therefore diverges between processes after a few dozen steps. The rules are unaffected, but step-by-step comparisons between runs are not meaningful.
IMPROVE_TEXT:
The Crafter score is a geometric mean, so achievements stuck near 0% cost the most. When an achievement is unlocked for the first time in an episode, we add β · (1 − p) to the reward, where p is the share of the last 200 episodes that unlocked it. With β = 2, a common achievement keeps roughly its +1 and one the agent has never managed is worth +3. The score is still computed from the unmodified game. It is about 30 lines (RarityBonus in train.py, flag --rarity_bonus).

We wrote the prediction down before the first run: stone pickaxe, iron and eat plant would rise above zero. The first two did, in every configuration. Iron tools were made only in bonus runs, a handful of times. Eat plant and diamonds stayed at zero: eating a plant means planting a sapling and coming back hundreds of steps later, which a bonus cannot teach if the agent never does it once. The price is sleep: waking up drops from about 88% to 70% of episodes, because the agent spends that time on the tech tree.

  • PPO, 3 seeds: 15.75 → 18.58 (β = 1) → 20.99 (β = 2) → 20.14 (β = 4). About 1.3 hours per run.
  • Achievement Distillation, seed 0: 17.71 → 22.80 (β = 1) → 23.08 (β = 2). About 7 hours per run.
  • With AD, β = 2 starts slower than β = 1. It trails until about 600k steps, then overtakes it once the stone pickaxe takes off (63% of recent episodes at 780k steps, against 51%).

Seed 0 is unusually bad for the baselines, so the AD gain on that seed is probably larger than typical. The cleanest evidence is the three-seed PPO sweep. The next step would be two more AD seeds per arm, about 28 GPU-hours on this laptop.
REPRO:
# Windows, from the repo root (game sources and .venv are recreated by the setup script)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/setup_windows.ps1

# Achievement Distillation, paper config, 1M steps (~7 h on an RTX 3050 Laptop)
.venv/Scripts/python methods/05_achievement_distillation/train.py --config ppo_ad --seed 0 --micro_batch 256 --aux_micro_batch 128

# the same with the rarity bonus (our change, best at beta = 2)
.venv/Scripts/python methods/05_achievement_distillation/train.py --config ppo_ad --seed 0 --micro_batch 256 --aux_micro_batch 128 --rarity_bonus 2.0 --run_name ad-rarity2-s0

# PPO and PPO + rarity bonus, seeds 0-2, back to back (~1.3 h per run)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/queue.ps1 -Config ppo -Bonus 0 -Prefix ppo -Seeds 0,1,2
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/queue.ps1 -Config ppo -Bonus 2.0 -Prefix ppo-rarity2 -Seeds 0,1,2

# live dashboard (http://localhost:8765) and periodic checkpoint videos
.venv/Scripts/python scripts/dashboard.py
.venv/Scripts/python scripts/spectator.py ad-ppo_ad-s0

# plots and summary table into results/
.venv/Scripts/python scripts/plot_results.py ppo-s0 ppo-rarity2-s0 ad-ppo_ad-s0 ad-rarity1-s0 ad-rarity2-s0
.venv/Scripts/python scripts/aggregate_seeds.py ppo ppo-rarity1 ppo-rarity2 ppo-rarity4 ad-ppo_ad ad-rarity1 ad-rarity2 --html runs/report/seeds.html --beta ppo=0 ppo-rarity1=1 ppo-rarity2=2 ppo-rarity4=4 --plot
FOOTER: 15 runs of 1M steps, 36 hours of training in total, on one RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (4 GB) with a Core i5-12500H. Crafter 1.8.3, Achievement-Distillation @ 9abbce6 with the paper's hyperparameters, PyTorch 2.11 + CUDA 12.8, Python 3.13. Code, logs and the work log are in the crafter_rl repository under methods/05_achievement_distillation, results/ and paper/work_log.md.

SEEDS_TEXT: The three PPO seeds average 15.75, almost exactly the paper's 15.60, so the setup reproduces the published baseline. The bonus helps in proportion to its strength up to β = 2 and then levels off. At β = 1 the gain is uneven: +7.9, +1.7 and −1.1 seed by seed, large when the baseline gets stuck before the stone pickaxe and gone when it finds the pickaxe on its own. At β = 2 it is +8.4, +3.5 and +3.7, so every seed improves. The mean rises to 20.99 and the spread between seeds shrinks from 3.0 to 0.9. At β = 4 the mean drops slightly, to 20.14. Three seeds per arm is still a small sample (paired t = 3.3 for β = 2). AD has one seed per arm, because each AD run takes 7 hours.
